plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in East Asian gardens and is celebrated in art and poetry for blooming in the cold tail end of winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Japan, China, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a symbol of perseverance and hope in East Asia because they bloom while snow may still be on the ground.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with nodding, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It naturalizes in woodlands and lawns and is among the first bulbs to flower as winter ends.
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce a compound called galantamine, which is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: An evergreen Australian tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden ball-shaped flower clusters. Although its main flowering peaks in late winter and spring, scattered blooms and related wattles continue in many regions, and it is a hardy ornamental.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to October); some wattle species flower sporadically in late summer
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up leafless stalks topped with clusters of fragrant, funnel-shaped pink flowers in the late Southern Hemisphere summer. Leaves appear only after the flowers fade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn in the Southern Hemisphere (February to April)
plants.location: Western Cape of South Africa; naturalized in Australia, California and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: The 'naked lady' nickname comes from its flower stalks emerging bare, without any leaves, from dry ground.
